title: Undo as a Tree
subtitle: {key:g}{key:-} and {key:g}{key:+} walk by time. `:undolist` shows the branches.
summary: Vim's undo is a tree. Every undo branch is preserved. {key:g}{key:-} and {key:g}{key:+} walk by chronological time; `:undolist` shows the branches; `:earlier` and `:later` jump through time.

blocks.text: Ordinary {key:u} and {key:Ctrl-R} are enough until history branches. The branch appears when you undo several changes and then make a different change. Many editors discard the old redo path at that moment. Vim keeps both futures.

That design extends the fearless editing model. A speculative edit does not have to destroy the path you abandoned. Vim records the new experiment as another branch, and the chronological commands can still reach the older states.

blocks.title: The Tree Structure
blocks.text:
Each change -- one insert session, one deletion, one substitution -- creates a node in the undo tree. {key:u} walks toward the parent of the current node; {key:Ctrl-R} walks toward its most recent child.

When you edit, undo, then edit again, the new edit becomes a new branch. The previous redo path survives as a sibling. Without {key:g}{key:-} and {key:g}{key:+}, that sibling is difficult to reach.

{key:g}{key:-} and {key:g}{key:+} walk by creation time rather than tree shape, so they can cross branches. `:undolist` shows the leaves of the tree with their sequence numbers, timestamps, and save numbers. `:undo {N}` jumps to a particular sequence number. `:earlier 5m` and `:later 30s` navigate by wall-clock time.

With `undofile` enabled, Vim saves undo history when the file is written and restores it in a later session. Neovim enables persistent undo only when your configuration turns the option on. The `undodir` option controls where those undo files live.
Plugins such as *undotree* draw the branches in a sidebar. The history already exists inside Vim; the plugin makes its shape easier to inspect.

blocks.title: Undo Is a Directed Graph
blocks.text: Linear edits build a chain of undo nodes. An edit after an undo creates a branch. {key:u} and {key:Ctrl-R} walk one chain; {key:g}{key:-} and {key:g}{key:+} walk by chronological time across branches; `:earlier` and `:later` walk by wall-clock time. The buffer state is reconstructed from the selected node rather than from a single destructive stack.
